searchText: <timbeiko> > <timbeiko> How much can this be compressed with another serialization method? (re @kevaundray: From this, I don't think we can allow people with 2G connections to participate (See serialisation section), since it would take them too much time to download the json file. I computed it at around 10-20 minutes with a 8-16Kilobytes per second speed, a binary file brings it down to 3-6 minutes but this is still pretty high imo) <timbeiko> Could you have the coordinator encode/decode to json (and prove they did it correctly)? <CarlBeek> the powers themselves are pseudo random, so we can only compress the data surrounding them <CarlBeek> so an efficient binary representation or a well compressed version of the powers should be close to the same size <timbeiko> got it <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> You might be able to do file compression, though this does add extra complexity to the contributor because they need to have that decompression algorithm (re @timbeiko: How much can this be compressed with another serialization method?) <timbeiko> I was trying to check what the most used smartphones are really quick to get specs but it seems hard to find 😅 <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Ah in the rationale, I proposed in the comments to use Samsung galaxy A13. The reason was because there is another competition whom are targetting roughly the same demographic and they chose this phone as the model (re @timbeiko: I was trying to check what the most used smartphones are really quick to get specs but it seems hard to find 😅) <kevaundray> I checked its specs and it does seem pretty powerful, so I'm not convinced I made the right choice there <timbeiko> right yeah, it seems like a pretty modern phone <timbeiko> but I guess if we are bandwidth limited, then maybe just checking for % of the world with 3G access could be good? <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Yeah thats a good point (re @timbeiko: but I guess if we are bandwidth limited, then maybe just checking for % of the world with 3G access could be good?) <timbeiko> https://www.statista.com/statistics/1228787/3g-mobile-network-coverage-worldwide-by-region/ <timbeiko> Africa is the worst continent for 3G coverage but still has 82% <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Do you think that thats enough for us to say that we can ignore 2G? (re @timbeiko: Africa is the worst continent for 3G coverage but still has 82%) <timbeiko> I’d want to dig a bit more into it - just found this but I don’t have the time to skim more: https://www.gsma.com/r/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/The-State-of-Mobile-Internet-Connectivity-Report-2021.pdf <timbeiko> a very cursory look suggests that most non-3G usage in Sub-Saharan Africa isn’t 2G but “feature phones” which couldn’t contribute anyways <timbeiko> <timbeiko> Page 50 seems to have some interesting nuance 🙂 <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Data-only devices means 2G here? (re @timbeiko: ) <timbeiko> > <timbeiko> I doubt it - wouldn’t be 12% in high income countries I think? (re @kevaundray: Data-only devices means 2G here?) <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Reading that it seems that disallowing 2G connections would completely restrict particular areas like congo (re @timbeiko: Page 50 seems to have some interesting nuance 🙂) <timbeiko> I read that differently 😛: even in their worst case examples, 3G penetration is still 50%+ and 2G users seem to care about “voice rather than data”, so would be unlikely to participate? <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> I was reading that 2G is also used for IoT, so maybe thats why its high in those countries. Though I'm not sure (re @timbeiko: I doubt it - wouldn’t be 12% in high income countries I think?) <timbeiko> Other interseting stat re: Congo is 4G going from 11%->42%, increasing by more than 3G over the same period, which could imply “people who want to use data are moving to more recent tech" <timbeiko> One thing which would make me more confident to completely drop 2G is figuring out how easy it is for someone in, say, Congo, to find someone else with a 3G phone they can use? <timbeiko> because you don’t need every user to have a device, you need them to have _access_ to one <CarlBeek> yeah i think this is a very reasonable assumption <timbeiko> that might also be something we can emphasize in the docs, e.g. it’s safe to have many people share the same device and each make a distinct contribution <CarlBeek> you could mobile-tether many devices to one phone too. <timbeiko> oh, like 2G devices being tethered to 3GB ones? <CarlBeek> well it is unlikely a 2G only device would be able to do the calculations in time anyway <CarlBeek> but yeah, a computer of the 2G era connected to a 3G device <CarlBeek> keep in mind that we open ourselves to a low-and-slow attack precisely to the degree that we allow for the slowest contributors. in the worst case, every contributor purposefully takes the longest allowable time to respond and that means the overall throughput is limited. (although functionally i don't for-see too much congestion, just temporarily so).
